Every :DOWN pattern in the four files: haiku-1 line 119: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^subscriber, :normal}; line 133: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^subscriber, :boom}; line 144: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^subscriber, :normal}. haiku-2 line 115: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :killed}; line 172: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal}. sonnet-1 line 166: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^subscriber, :killed}; line 181: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^subscriber, :normal}. sonnet-2 line 52: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal}; line 58: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :killed}. Ten patterns, every one matching the reason the test caused (send :stop -> :normal, Process.exit(_, :kill) -> :killed, Process.exit(_, :boom) -> :boom); none uses _ or a bound variable. The sentence is broken by 0 of 4 runs. Before it, check-6 had the shape in 2 of 4 (haiku-2 line 66 and sonnet-1 line 195: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, _reason}), then graded clean. sonnet-2's transcript shows it rewriting a ^reason pattern into :killed with sed before finishing.

Changed rule (uncommitted): "Assert with patterns" (references/testing.md) gained the sentence that now decides its bare-match verdicts: "In a test body, put `assert` in front of a match: a bare `{:ok, pid} = start(...)` fails as a `MatchError` without the assertion's formatted value." Counted: a match with a refutable left side (a literal, tuple, list or map) written without assert inside a test block. Not counted: bindings to a plain variable (ref = Process.monitor(pid), subscriber = spawn_subscriber()) and _ = :sys.get_state(server) / _ = Subscriptions.subscribers(...), which cannot fail; matches in setup blocks and helper or TestMailer functions, which are not test bodies (every run's setup has {:ok, _owner} = Registry.register(...), the skill's own example shape). Per run: haiku-1 0 bare matches in test bodies (arrange calls are unmatched, e.g. line 49: Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self()); asserted calls use assert, line 39: assert :ok = Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self())); haiku-2 22, all :ok = calls (lines 39, 45, 46, 55, 63, 70, 72, 78, 79, 81, 88, 90, 101, 111, 121, 122, 132, 133, 142, 143, 146, 155; quoted in its verdict); sonnet-1 0 (unmatched arrange calls such as line 61: Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", "ada@example.com") and assert :ok = for the call under test, line 49); sonnet-2 26, all :ok = calls (lines 77, 83, 84, 97, 98, 99, 108, 110, 116, 118, 124, 126, 133, 134, 136, 152, 153, 155, 162, 163, 165, 178, 179, 181, 215, 229; quoted in its verdict), plus three more in the describe-level setup at lines 192-194 that are not counted. All use async: true with a setup_all Registry keyed by Module.concat(module, test) and a behaviour-implementing TestMailer that finds the test pid through Process.info(self(), :registered_name); every server is start_supervised! under that name; sonnet-1 (lines 38-43) and sonnet-2 (lines 63-67) assert the missing-mailer failure with start_supervised/1 under a separate test-specific name and match the KeyError reason; subscriber helpers are bare spawn/1 processes (graded clean as before); refutes follow a synchronous call (:sys.get_state/1 or subscribers/2) or later assert_receives from the same sender; no Process.register, application env, start_link call, elem/2, import or require. Process.sleep(:infinity) at sonnet-1 line 160 keeps a subscriber alive and is not counted; sonnet-2 line 223: assert Process.alive?(server) is one assertion after a :DOWN wait, not polling. Directive order: haiku-1 line 18 use / lines 20-21 alias, alias; haiku-2 line 21 use / line 23 alias Notify.{Subscriptions, TestMailer}; sonnet-1 line 19 use / lines 21-22 alias, alias; sonnet-2 line 23 use / lines 25-26 alias, alias; no test module has a @moduledoc, the directives open the body, and the TestMailer modules have none.
